source: Human-reviewed xref2 benchmark cases; expected behavioral regressions reconstructed from the callee implementations and PR intent.

xref2-case-a.description: op_one raises ErrorA for a missing key, but the changed handler removed the ErrorA catch and now only checks for None.

xref2-case-b.description: op_two sorts and removes duplicates in place, so passing raw mutates the caller's input before its length is logged.

xref2-case-c.description: The retry loop performs an additional op_three call after the third failed notification, causing an unintended fourth store mutation.

xref2-case-d.description: op_four wraps filesystem failures in ErrorB, but the changed handler catches FileNotFoundError instead.

xref2-case-e.description: op_five returns a generator; the first sum consumes it, so the second sum produces zero after the list materialization was removed.

xref2-case-f.description: One Helper instance with an unsynchronized counter is shared across ThreadPoolExecutor workers, allowing the cap to be exceeded.

xref2-case-g.description: The caller converts the ratio to percent and op_seven multiplies by 100 again, producing a value scaled twice.

xref2-case-h.description: op_eight can mutate or raise before the log append, so the record is not logged when the operation fails.
